tossups.question: This composer’s works for piano four-hands include a Grand Duo piano sonata and a Fantasia in F minor posthumously dedicated to Caroline Esterházy. The final three of this composer’s 21 piano sonatas are found near the end of the Deutsch catalog of his works. Rachmaninoff took the title of his six Moments Musicaux from this composer of the collection Schwanengesang (“SHVAH-nin-guh-zong”) and the difficult C-major Wanderer Fantasy. Thundering octave-G triplets in a lied (“leet”) by this composer accompany cries of “Mein Vater” from a boy who is killed by the title figure on a frantic nighttime ride. For 10 points, name this Austrian composer of “Erlkönig” and the Unfinished Symphony.

In a novel by this author, a girl sits for a portrait while an artist secretly sculpts a life-size replica of her body. A man in a novel by this author fires two Jewish housemaids due to his commitment to dignity. Miss Emily explains that “deferrals” don’t exist in a novel titled for a Judy Bridgewater song, written by this author of Klara and the Sun. In a novel by this author, Tommy “completes” after leaving Hailsham with Ruth and Kathy, who are clones made for organ donation. In a novel by this author, Mr. Farraday purchases Darlington Hall, the workplace of the butler Stevens. For 10 points, name this Japanese-British author of Never Let Me Go and The Remains of the Day.

The holiest festival in a religion from this modern-day country takes place in the month of Jalal and is named for the Garden of Ridvan. Wilmette, Illinois houses the oldest remaining temple of a religion from this modern-day country that reveres the phrase “He whom God shall make manifest” from the Bayan. In a religion from this modern-day country, the Chinvat Bridge must be crossed by souls, whose dead bodies are placed on Towers of Silence. Adherents of a religion in this modern-day country jump over bonfires before the New Year’s holiday of Nowruz (“noh-ROOZ”). For 10 points, Baha’i (“bah-HAH-ee”) and Zoroastrianism were founded in what modern-day country centered at Tehran?

A poem by this non-Greek author provides the framework for Matthew Arnold’s poem “Thyrsis” and depicts Corydon winning a singing contest. In the tenth and final poem of a collection by this author, Cornelius Gallus imagines dying in Arcadia before delivering the line “Love conquers all.” Aristaeus (“ar-iss-TAY-us”) discovers beekeeping in an epyllion from this author’s Georgics. In a long poem by this author, the Sibyl of Cumae (“KOO-mye”) helps a character reach the underworld. Augustus ordered the preservation of a poem by this author whose title character flees the sack of Troy and abandons Dido in Carthage. For 10 points, name this Roman poet of the Eclogues and the Aeneid.

This leader’s wife Carmen Polo headed the Women’s Protection Board, which incarcerated women they believed had violated the values of National Catholicism. This leader’s Stabilization Plan led to an economic miracle in his country. This leader’s country followed the Pact of Forgetting to avoid confronting his legacy, which included forcing prisoners of war to build the Valley of the Fallen during his White Terror. In Operation Ogre, one of this leader’s prime ministers was blasted over a five-story church by the ETA. Under this caudillo’s (“kao-DEE-yo”) regime, the Falange (“fah-LAHN-hay”) was the only legal political party. For 10 points, what dictator led the Nationalists in the Spanish Civil War?
tossups.answer: Francisco Franco [or Francisco Franco Bahamonde; or Francisco Paulino Hermenegildo Teódulo Franco Bahamonde]

tossups.question: The use of iodine doping to produce conductive types of these molecules won Heeger, MacDiarmid, and Shirakawa the 2000 Nobel in Chemistry. These molecules’ orientations remain correlated over their persistence length. Azo compounds like AIBN may decompose into radicals to initiate the production of these molecules. Samples of these molecules approach a dispersity of 2 under ideal step-growth. Chains of these molecules are connected by crosslinks. PVC and Teflon are examples of these molecules, which are the main component of plastics. For 10 points, name these molecules composed of repeating units called monomers.

In a painting by this artist commissioned by Ithiel Town, a green curtain frames a young man reclining atop a column. This artist depicted himself sitting on a rock and looking back at the viewer in a painting in which tree stumps spell “Noah” in Hebrew. This painter of The Architect’s Dream stands on a rock ledge next to William Cullen Bryant in the Catskill Mountains in Asher Durand's Kindred Spirits. A view from Mount Holyoke (“HO-lee-oak”) titles a painting by this artist that depicts a bend in the Connecticut River. For 10 points, name this painter of The Oxbow and founder of the Hudson River School.

Floods of this river create wetlands called várzea forests. Early settlements on this river are exemplified by the Marajó (“mah-rah-ZHOO”) culture, which is named for an island in this river. The Xingu (“shing-GOO”) River is a tributary of this river where explorer Percy Fawcett was last reported during his search for the Lost City of Z. The rubber industry helped grow the city of Manaus (“mah-NAUSS”), which lies on the confluence of this river and the Rio Negro. The Arapaima is native to this river, which is home to the most piranha species on Earth. For 10 points, name this river with the largest discharge volume that runs through a rainforest in Brazil.

Cyprian and Novatian disagreed on how to deal with some of these people, who avoided punishment by becoming lapsi (“LAHP-see”). Tertullian was one of the earliest to defend these people in Latin, including from charges of child sacrifice. In response to Arianism, Theodosius I passed the Edict of Thessalonica to bolster a creed for these people adopted at the Council of Nicaea. The Edict of Milan ended the state persecution of this group. A vision of the Greek letters chi and rho before the Battle of Milvian Bridge partly caused Constantine I to join this group on his deathbed. For 10 points, the Roman punishment of crucifixion led to what religious group venerating the cross?
tossups.answer: Roman Christians [or Christiani; accept Catholics; accept Arians until “Arius” is read; prompt on martyrs; prompt on ethnicities like Greeks or Romans by asking “in what social group?”]

tossups.question: Undoing an action performed on these systems usually requires the user to write out a compensation log record. Edgar Codd formalized a system of algebra that models operations on these systems. Executions performed on these systems must be “all or nothing” according to the principle of atomicity. Transactions performed on these systems should often obey the ACID (“acid”) properties. These systems are manipulated by a language that uses keywords like SELECT and MERGE to access them. The “relational” kind of these systems can be queried by SQL (“sequel”). For 10 points, name these organized collections of electronic data.
tossups.answer: databases [or DBs; accept relational databases; prompt on datatables by asking “within what systems”]

tossups.question: In a play by this author, a character uses his bus fare to play Sarah Vaughan’s song “Little Man You’ve Had a Busy Day” on the jukebox. This author founded the Serpent Players with John Kani and Winston Ntshona (“un-CHO-nah”). This author created a character who puts a copy of On the Origin of Species in the theology section and later writes the essay “A World Without Collisions.” In a play by this author, a boy tells a man, “You can’t fly kites on rainy days,” after earlier spitting in his face. That play opens and closes with the Black servants Sam and Willie ballroom dancing. For 10 points, name this South African playwright of Master Harold… and the Boys.

This process is the subject of the “Tropics as a Museum” hypothesis. Leigh Van Valen posited that the probability of this process occurring was constant over time in the Red Queen hypothesis. Neighboring groups can prevent this process’ namesake “vortices” in metapopulations via the rescue effect. This process is incorrectly thought to have occurred in Lazarus taxa, as exemplified by coelacanths (“SEE-luh-canths”). The Permian–Triassic boundary exemplifies the “mass” version of this process. For 10 points, overhunting can lead to what process where all members of a species die out?
tossups.answer: extinction [accept word forms such as going extinct; accept extinction vortices; accept mass extinction; accept Permian–Triassic extinction or Permian extinction or Late Permian extinction or End-Permian extinction; prompt on Great Dying; prompt on dying out or die out until read]

tossups.question: Conan Gray contributed backing vocals to a song by this singer which states “I hope I never see what your face looks like going.” After performing “Friday I’m in Love” with him at Glastonbury, this singer featured Robert Smith in a song describing how she “Went to the doctor and she said I was fine.” This singer described her friends “smoking blunts in the bathroom” in a song that states, “You’re a spark in the dark and my clothes all caught aflame.” A 2026 album by this artist includes the songs “what’s wrong with me” and “honeybee.” For 10 points, the album you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love is by what singer of “drivers license”?

In a story by this author, the narrator raps his cane on his “[emphasize] excellently well constructed house” before hearing an “anomalous and inhuman” howl. In another story by this author, a character produces a trowel to prove he’s a mason to a character with a concerning cough, and has the family motto “Nemo me impune lacessit” (“NAY-moh may im-POO-nay lah-KES-sit”). The narrator of a story by this author kills his wife with an ax because she prevents him from killing the title “Black Cat.” In a story by this author that concludes “In pace requiescat!” (“in PAH-chay reck-wee-ESS-caht”), a character cries, “For the love of God, Montresor!” before being buried alive in the catacombs. For 10 points, name this Gothic author of “The Cask of Amontillado.”

Wiley Thompson was killed by a leader in this present-day state with the very rifle he gifted him. Two British subjects were executed in this state, igniting the Arbuthnot–Ambrister affair. This state’s Negro Fort housed maroons, some of whom later became known as “Black” members of one tribe. The treaties of Moultrie Creek and Payne’s Landing forcibly relocated a tribe in this state, which was transferred to the United States in the Adams–Onís Treaty. Andrew Jackson fought an 1817 to 1818 war named for a tribe in this state that was later led by Chief Osceola. For 10 points, name this state where the Seminole Wars were fought around the Everglades.

While disguised as an eagle, this god defecated a substance made from blood and honey. In one poem, this god may be manifested as High, Just-As-High, and Third. This god transformed into a snake to slip into a mountain and slept with a woman for three nights to steal the Mead of Poetry. This god’s wolves, Geri and Freki, dine with the einherjar (“ain-HAIR-yar”) in a “Hall of the Slain” presided over by this god. At Ragnarok, Fenrir will devour this wielder of Gungnir. The severed head of Mimir advises this god, who learned the runes by hanging from a tree for nine nights. For 10 points, name this leader of the Aesir, the one-eyed “All-Father” of Norse mythology.

This scientist built a clay model of the U-V-S surface of an imaginary water-like substance. The thermodynamic square can be used to recall a set of relations named for this physicist between first-order partial derivatives. This physicist derived a statistical distribution for velocities in ideal gases that was later generalized by Boltzmann. Only fast-moving particles can pass through a gate in a thought experiment violating the second law of thermodynamics known as this physicist’s “demon.” Gauss’s and Ampère’s laws are among a set of four coupled equations named after this physicist. For 10 points, what Scotsman names four equations governing electromagnetism?

A musician with this surname released the album Translinear Light after a 25-year hiatus. The name Turiyasangitananda (“too-REE-yah-sung-it-ah-NUN-dah”) was adopted by a harpist with this surname after she released the album Journey in Satchidananda (“sut-chit-AH-nun-duh”). A song by a musician with this surname uses tonic centers of B, G, and E-flat, which are each a major third apart. A gong clash opens the track “Psalm” by an artist with this surname who developed the “sheets of sound” technique. Moves by major thirds are the namesake “changes” of an artist with this surname, as heard in Giant Steps. For 10 points, give this surname of the saxophonist behind A Love Supreme, with first name John.
tossups.answer: Coltrane [accept Alice Coltrane or John Coltrane; prompt on McLeod by asking “what was her married surname?”]

tossups.question: This text’s author defended its contrast of appetite and aversion as the basic driving forces of “vital” and “voluntary” motion while debating Bishop John Bramhall. The main causes of war are competition, glory, and diffidence according to this text, which deems the fear of violent death the summum malum, or greatest evil, of life. A “Confederacy of Deceivers” forms the title “Kingdom of Darkness” of one section of this text. This text argues that a “war of all against all” characterizes the state of nature, which leaves life “solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short.” For 10 points, a biblical sea monster names what magnum opus of Thomas Hobbes?
tossups.answer: Leviathan [or Leviathan: Or the Matter, Forme and Power of a Commonwealth, Ecclesiasticall and Civil]

tossups.question: The return of an exiled president to this city was interrupted when snipers opened fire on a crowd gathered at a rally near its main airport. A man under the alias Ricardo Klement took a ratline to this city, where a so-called “Liberating Revolution” overthrew the founder of the Justicialist Party. The Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo were founded in this city to protest forced disappearances by the National Reorganization Process during the Dirty War. A leader who ruled from this city was supported by descamisados and married the actress Evita. For 10 points, from what city did Juan Perón govern Argentina?
tossups.answer: Buenos Aires (Adolf Eichmann took the alias Ricardo Klement.)

bonuses.leadin: In a novel written in this language, Diadorim is revealed to be a woman after dying in a knife fight with a rival bandit leader. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this language of the novel The Devil to Pay in the Backlands. In another novel written in this language, the doctor’s wife is unaffected by the title “white sickness.”
This Brazilian author used Portuguese to describe the existential crisis of the title character, who kills and eats a cockroach found in a wardrobe, in the novel The Passion According to G. H.

The Devil to Pay in the Backlands and The Passion According to G. H. are written using this narrative technique with a 3-word name, in which the story is told through the narrator’s uninterrupted flow of thoughts.
answers: Portuguese [or Português; or língua portuguesa] (The Devil to Pay in the Backlands is by João Guimarães Rosa; the unnamed novel is Blindness by José Saramago.)

bonuses.leadin: The action functional is found by integrating the Lagrangian, which is the difference between these two quantities. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these two quantities typically symbolized T and V. Adding these two quantities yields the Hamiltonian.
For a system of particles experiencing a power-law force, this theorem equates the time-average kinetic energy to a constant times the time-average total potential energy.
The constant in the gravitational virial theorem is the negative of this value. Kinetic energy equals this value times m-v-squared.

bonuses.leadin: At the start of a play by this author, the Logician describes a syllogism which falsely concludes that all beings with four paws are cats. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Absurdist author who wrote a play in which Bérenger (“bay-ron-ZHAY”) shouts “I’m not capitulating!” after resisting a transformation into a rhinoceros.
In another Ionesco play, Bérenger is a 400-year-old man with this title who has two wives, Marguerite and Marie. Ubu holds this title in an Alfred Jarry (“zhah-REE”) play.

Bérenger wakes up one day with this ability in Ionesco’s play A Stroll in the Air. Tinker Bell bestows this supernatural ability on Wendy, John, and Michael with pixie dust in J. M. Barrie’s play Peter Pan.
answers: king [or roi; accept king of Poland; accept Ubu Roi or King Ubu; accept Exit the King or Le Roi se meurt]
flight [accept word forms like flying; accept word forms of defying gravity]

bonuses.leadin: Because this figure played the tackle sport kabaddi (“KUH-bud-dee”) in his youth, many Tibetan and Japanese monks still engage in the sport today. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this religious figure who achieved enlightenment under a Bodhi tree and was born with the name Siddhartha Gautama (“sid-ARR-thuh GAU-tuh-muh”).

Though he was okay with playing kabaddi, the Buddha listed 16 kinds of games he would not play, including a game of guessing these things traced by a finger. Four of these things comprise the Tetragrammaton.
Like Siddhartha, this figure may have also played kabaddi in his youth. The gopis (“GO-pees”) are devotees of this figure, one of whom is his consort Radha (“RAH-dah”).
answers: letters [or characters; accept Brahmi letters; accept Hebrew letters; prompt on alphabets]
Krishna [or Krsna; accept Krishna Janmāshṭamī; accept Govinda; or Madhava; or Gopala; prompt on Vishnu]

bonuses.leadin: This polity incorporated the Duchy of Livonia into its realm during the Livonian War. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this polity that officially formed following the Union of Lublin. This polity’s Golden Liberty gave the liberum veto to all members of the Sejm (“same”).
The Livonian War began with an invasion by a Tsar of this name called the “Terrible.”
Polish involvement in the Livonian War began under Sigismund II Augustus, a king of this dynasty. The founder of this dynasty began ruling Poland after marrying Queen Jadwiga (“yahd-VEE-gah”).
answers: Poland–Lithuania [accept either underlined portion; accept Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; accept Grand Duchy of Lithuania]
Ivan [accept Ivan the Terrible or Ivan IV Vasilyevich or Ivan Grozny]

Jagiellonian (“yog-yell-OH-nee-in”) Dynasty [or dynastia jagiellońska; or Jogailaičių dinastija; or House of Jagiello; or Dom Jagiellonów; accept Jogailaičiai; accept Jagiellonowie; prompt on House of Gediminas; prompt on Gediminids]

bonuses.leadin: In 2023, Casgevy, a treatment for this disease, became the first FDA-approved CRISPR-based gene therapy. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this disease, which results from a glutamate-to-valine point substitution in hemoglobin. Vaso-occlusive crises cause reduced oxygen flow and capillary damage in patients with this disease.

People with a single allele for the sickle-cell trait often have increased resistance to malaria in an example of this phenomenon, whereby having two different alleles for a given trait confers greater fitness.
Heterozygotes have one recessive allele and one allele with this property, often denoted with a capital letter.

bonuses.leadin: This sculptor’s series of Resting Satyr statues may have inspired a replica at the Capitoline Hill. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this sculptor who depicted a god holding a baby in his Hermes and the Infant Dionysus.
Praxiteles depicted this goddess in one of the first life-sized female nude sculptures. Alexandros of Antioch may have sculpted a now-armless marble statue named [this goddess] “de Milo.”

A series by Praxiteles depicting this figure as a lizard-killer includes one controversially held in Cleveland. Leochares (“lee-OCK-uh-reez”) depicted this figure in a sculpture located at Belvedere Court.
answers: Venus [or Aphrodite; accept Aphrodite of Knidos; accept Venus de Milo; accept Aphrodite of Melos]

bonuses.leadin: The protagonist of this video game sees her lover get shot by Nathan Prescott and rewinds time to prevent it. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this game set in the fictional town of Arcadia Bay. Chloe Price and Max Caulfield investigate Rachel Amber’s disappearance in this game.
Another way Max is able to time travel in Life is Strange is by focusing on one of these objects, which she prints from her Polaroid camera.
Before seeing Chloe get shot, Max takes a picture of a blue one of these insects. Silcoon evolves into a Pokémon named after one of these animals.
answers: Life is Strange [prompt on LiS; reject “Life is Strange 2” or “Life is Strange: Before the Storm”]
butterflies [accept Blue Butterfly; accept Butterfly Effect; prompt on Beautifly by asking “what animal is it based on?”; reject “moth”]

bonuses.leadin: This period arose partly in response to the “Great Darkness” of Maurice Duplessis’s conservatism. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this period of social transformation that began with the election of Jean Lesage (“luh-SAZH”) in 1960. The secularization of education decreased the Catholic Church’s influence in this period.
A 1949 strike by miners of this resource helped incite the Quiet Revolution. This heatproof building resource causes a kind of cancer called mesothelioma.

This politician, who supported the asbestos miners, passed the Official Languages Act during the Quiet Revolution. Pierre Laporte’s (“lah-PORT’s”) kidnapping caused this politician to invoke the War Measures Act.
answers: Pierre Trudeau [or Joseph Philippe Pierre Yves Elliott Trudeau; prompt on Trudeau; reject “Justin Trudeau”]

bonuses.leadin: Laura Mulvey (“MULL-vee”) described these people’s objectifying “gaze” in her essay “Visual Pleasure and Narrative Cinema.” For 10 points each:
parts: Name this gender of people often placed in positions of power in a patriarchy.

According to Mulvey, Hollywood films enable this condition in men and objectify women with scopophilia. This condition is characterized by symptoms like a pattern of grandiosity and a constant need for admiration.

Mulvey argues that the movie-going experience returns us to this developmental stage since the audience temporarily loses their ego. Jacques Lacan envisioned this stage in which children form an “I-function.”
answers: narcissism [accept word forms such as narcissistic; accept narcissistic personality disorder; prompt on NPD]

bonuses.leadin: Trumpeter Pete Candoli’s boast of having met Stravinsky may have led Woody Herman to commission the Ebony Concerto for this instrument and jazz band. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this single-reed woodwind instrument. Aaron Copland’s concerto for this instrument was written for jazz musician Benny Goodman.

The keys on a clarinet inspired the title of this composer’s Gnarly Buttons. This composer of the fanfare Short Ride in a Fast Machine described his piece The Chairman Dances as an “outtake” from one of his operas.

The second movement of Gnarly Buttons, “Mad Cow,” is in this dance form. A xylophone quotes the tune “Bonaparte’s Retreat” in an excerpt with this title from Rodeo (“roh-DAY-oh”), the last of Copland’s Four Dance Episodes.

bonuses.leadin: The work of the bard Taliesin may have been preserved in a manuscript from this country. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this country whose other mythical heroes include Brân the Blessed and Pryderi (“prih-DAIR-ee”), who both appear in this country’s myth collection, the Mabinogion (“mah-bih-NOG-yun”).
This Welsh queen and mother of Pryderi was framed for Pryderi’s murder by having blood smeared on her face according to the first of the Four Branches of the Mabinogion.

Outside of the Four Branches, the Mabinogion also contains tales about this legendary king of Britain whom Taliesin (“tal-YES-in”) may have served. This wielder of Excalibur was served by the Knights of the Round Table.
answers: Wales [or Cymru (“KUM-ree”); prompt on United Kingdom or UK; prompt on Great Britain; reject “England”]

bonuses.leadin: In a play titled for this woman, she hides in a rolled-up carpet to enter the Pharos lighthouse. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Egyptian queen who, in that play, is shown sleeping between the paws of a sphinx before meeting her lover Julius Caesar.

Caesar and Cleopatra is by this author, who posthumously funded the creation of a namesake 48-character alphabet. The phonetician Henry Sweet inspired a character who has slippers thrown at him in a play by this author.
In Shaw’s play Pygmalion, Eliza Doolittle throws slippers at this character, who is referred to as “The Note Taker” while in Covent Garden at the beginning of the play.
answers: Cleopatra VII [or Cleopatra VII Thea Philopator; accept Caesar and Cleopatra]

bonuses.leadin: This process involves producing a sheet of light-sensitive silver-plated copper to capture the image projected by a camera obscura. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this first publicly available photographic process, which is named for its French creator.
Daguerreotypes were used in the United States by this photographer, who displayed images of the US Civil War at his gallery during the exhibit The Dead of Antietam.

Mathew Brady described himself as under obligation to preserve the faces of historic men and [these people]. A woman and three children appear in a Dorothea Lange (“lang”) photo titled for a “Migrant” one of these family members.

bonuses.leadin: Pseudohistorian Gavin Menzies’s book 1421 claims that this admiral explored America before Columbus. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this admiral who collected a giraffe as tribute from the Swahili Coast. This Hui (“hway”) eunuch led the Míng Dynasty’s treasure voyages.
Zheng He’s treasure voyages began under this third Míng emperor. This emperor ordered the compilation of the world’s largest paper encyclopedia.
The Yongle Emperor moved the capital of the Míng Dynasty to this modern capital of China, where he began construction of the Forbidden City.
answers: Zheng He (“jung huh”) [or Cheng Ho; accept Ma He; accept San Bao or Sam Po]
Yongle (“YONG-luh”) Emperor [or Zhu Di; accept Yongle Encyclopedia or Yongle dadian; prompt on Zhu]

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following things related to testing a hypothesis about a distribution's mean, for 10 points each:
parts: One way is by using a test named for a ratio of this function. This function, which equals the joint probability density of observing data given a certain parameter, is maximized in a technique to estimate a parameter’s value.

A standard approach is to compare a test statistic against this distribution, with “n minus one” degrees of freedom. This distribution approaches the normal distribution as degrees of freedom approach infinity.
The test statistic for a mean hypothesis test is generated by dividing this quantity by the square root of “n.” This measure of spread is the square root of variance.

bonuses.leadin: Matthew Bruccoli’s biography of this author is titled Some Sort of Epic Grandeur. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this author who wrote about Nick Carraway’s relationship with the title party host in The Great Gatsby.

Bruccoli described hunting for a copy of The Great Gatsby after hearing a radio broadcast of this Fitzgerald novella. Kismine escapes before Braddock Washington blows up a mountain at the end of this novella.

This character from The Great Gatsby is reimagined as a Vietnamese immigrant with magical powers in Nghi Vo’s (“nee vo’s”) novel The Chosen and the Beautiful. Nick briefly dates this cheating golf champion.
answers: F. Scott Fitzgerald [or Francis Scott Key Fitzgerald; accept Some Sort of Epic Grandeur: The Life of F. Scott Fitzgerald]

bonuses.leadin: This element’s oxide and silicate are the primary components of Pyrex glass. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this element that may form unusual three-center two-electron bonds due to being “electron-deficient.” This group 3 element is the lightest metalloid.

Pyrex is notable for being able to resist this process, thus reducing the buildup of internal stresses. Linear and volumetric parameters symbolized alpha and beta characterize this process, which causes bimetallic strips to bend.

Pyrex is used in laboratory glassware, such as this type of equipment that often features a round bottom. Solutions are often held in beakers or these glass containers, one type of which is named for Emil Erlenmeyer.
answers: thermal expansion [accept linear coefficient of thermal expansion; accept volumetric coefficient of thermal expansion]

bonuses.leadin: Grandfather clauses shielded poor whites from restrictions on this right. For 10 points each:
parts: Literacy tests infringed upon what right that was granted to Black Americans by the 15th Amendment?

Wade Hampton III was supported by a group named for these objects that suppressed Black voters in the South. Radical Republicans who invoked Civil War death tolls were often accused of “waving” one of these objects.
This Oliver Otis Howard-led organization helped mobilize Black voters in the South. Andrew Johnson opposed this Reconstruction-era organization that provided support to a namesake group of people.
answers: shirts [accept “waving the bloody shirt”; accept bloody shirts; accept red shirts]
Freedmen’s Bureau [accept Bureau of Refugees, Freedmen, and Abandoned Lands]

bonuses.leadin: In The Attainment of Happiness, Al-Farabi claimed that “flourishing” required mastering four types of these qualities, including their “deliberative” and “theoretical” forms. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these qualities that lie on a “golden mean” between two extremes according to Nicomachean Ethics.

This scholar linked “theoretical” virtues to the “theoretical part” of the ideal political system. In a dialogue responding to Al-Ghazali, this Andalusian scholar defended a synthesis of Islamic thought and virtue ethics.
Averroes became known as “The Commentator” for his extensive commentaries on this student of Plato, who originated virtue ethics in his Nicomachean Ethics.
answers: moral virtues [or areté or akhlaq; accept theoretical virtues or deliberative virtues]
Averroes (“uh-VAIR-roh-eez”) [or Abu al-Walid Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Rushd] (Averroes authored The Incoherence of the Incoherence as a critique of Al-Ghazali’s The Incoherence of the Philosophers.)
